equations.printed: Heat-flux magnitude Q = thermal conductivity c × geothermal gradient dT/dz.
equations.check: W/m2 = (W/m/K)×(K/m). Temperature differences convert with5/9, no32offset. Positive magnitude versus signed Fourier flux requires a coordinate convention. Constant-c assumption is local; c range1.5–6W/m/K means heat-flow and gradient ratios are not generally identical across sediments. Independent endpoint/unit checks do not reconstruct a thermal reservoir model.

equations.printed: No governing compositional-flow, flash/EOS, Gaussian-geostatistical, structural-riser or well-pressure equations are supplied; commercial GEM/GHG and qualitative outcomes are described.
equations.check: Model names/parameter ranges are insufficient for independent reproduction. Relative permeability, capillarity, compositional/PVT/salinity, heat transfer, pressure boundaries, grid dimensions, fracture controls, variograms/seeds, structural loads and convergence/mass-balance results remain open.

variables: Q is heat-flux magnitude inW/m2; c is thermal conductivity inW/m/K; dT/dz is geothermal gradient inK/m. The sign convention is not specified. Conductivity spans 1.5–6 W/m/K; site-to-site constancy is not established.

Seafloor temperature is 35 F; gradients are 6/6/2 F per 100 ft. Constant-gradient continuation to328 ft gives54.68/54.68/41.56 F. These are conditional calculations, not recovered GEM cell temperatures.

Seabed pressures4150/4405/8120 psi and deep-case5450 psi have unspecified gauge/absolute datums. They are not fracture limits, wellhead controls or allowed BHPs; pressure/depth ratios do not establish injection headroom.

The 25×25×60 grid has37,500 cells. The injection well is centred at i=j=13 and completed in lower blocks. Lateral spacing, physical extent, vertical layering and exact completed k indices are unavailable.

Porosity ranges are 60–80/42–66/67–83%; permeability ranges are 0.1–40/7.5–18.5/0.002–1.6 mD. Two microD equals 0.002 mD. Ranges and unconditional Gaussian generation do not specify realised fields, anisotropy, variograms, seeds or cross-correlation.
Table 3 describes site 3 as pelagic siliceous ooze; page 11 calls it lithogenous. Preserve both labels without inventing a mineral, thermal-property or core-data join.

Each case imposes 5,000 reported tons/day for 25 years, then stops injection for 225 years. Tons are unqualified; no metric/short-ton conversion. No availability loss, measured acceptance or pressure-constrained maximum is established.

The 7-inch casing conveyance estimate is 3,000 tons/day; perforations span10–30 ft. Outside diameter does not determine internal diameter, wall, roughness, velocity or hydraulic loss. An imposed5,000 tons/day does not validate the well.

Ship capacity is described at a 500,000ft3 scale. Nearshore100-million and far-offshore10-million-ton annual claims lack density, fill, fleet, cycle, maintenance and weather parameters. Preferred port distance<=200 miles is not an actual route measurement.

Riser check marks depend on material, outside diameter, depth and weather category. Loads, stresses, fatigue/acceptance criteria, return-period parameters and operational availability are not supplied.

Figures 7–8 show global CO2 mole fraction, not phase saturation, mobile mass or retained fraction. Their positive1e-5 colour floor and finite 250-year snapshots do not demonstrate exact zero or indefinite permanence.
Narrative red-zone boxes of 2×2×6,3×3×7 and4×4×8 give approximate cell counts only. Unequal pore volumes, densities and compositions prevent converting them to CO2 mass or retention.

Page 4 gives approximate supercritical thresholds above 1070 psi and88 F. The page 13 statement at>=80 F does not meet that temperature condition at 80 F. Phase and brine-relative density require separate verification.

The additional3,000-ft case reports200 F/5450 psi. It needs a domain distinct from the principal328-ft sediment models. The complete temperature field is not recovered by continuing an average gradient.
The source calls the pore fluid air+seawater but does not supply its exact composition, salinity, EOS or property implementation. No generic freshwater/CO2 model substitutes for the author case.

Hydrates, displaced-fluid chemistry and earthquake/geomechanical perturbations require further study according to the authors. Their quantitative effects on acceptance and retention are not validated here.
